references.text: The elders of the city gather at the city gate to testify and handle legal matters, just as in the book of Ruth where Boaz goes to the city gate to arrange the right of redemption.
The kinsman-redeemer refuses to redeem, which mirrors the situation where a man refuses to fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law.
Onan refused to fulfill his duty toward his deceased brother's wife, an early example of refusing the levirate duty.
The preceding context explains the levirate marriage and what happens when a man refuses to take his deceased brother's widow.
The following text describes the consequences and the ritual when the man confirms that he will not marry the widow.
